question_text:
At what temperature will the diffusion coefficient for the diffusion of zinc in copper have a value of $2.6 \times$ $10^{-16} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{s}$? Use the diffusion data in  table 6.2 .

Table 6.2
A Tabulation of Diffusion Data
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Diffusing Species & Host Metal & $D_0\left(m^2 / s\right)$ & $Q_d(\mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol})$ \\
\hline \multicolumn{4}{|c|}{Interstitial Diffusion} \\
\hline $\mathrm{C}^b$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\alpha$ or BCC $){ }^a$ & $1.1 \times 10^{-6}$ & 87,400 \\
\hline $\mathrm{C}^c$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\gamma \text { or FCC })^a$ & $2.3 \times 10^{-5}$ & 148,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{N}^b$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\alpha$ or BCC$){ }^a$ & $5.0 \times 10^{-7}$ & 77,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{N}^c$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\gamma \text { or FCC })^a$ & $9.1 \times 10^{-5}$ & 168,000 \\
\hline & \multicolumn{3}{|c|}{Self-Diffusion} \\
\hline $\mathrm{Fe}^c$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\alpha$ or BCC $){ }^a$ & $2.8 \times 10^{-4}$ & 251,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Fe}^c$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\gamma \text { or FCC })^a$ & $5.0 \times 10^{-5}$ & 284,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Cu}^d$ & Cu (FCC) & $2.5 \times 10^{-5}$ & 200,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Al}^c$ & Al (FCC) & $2.3 \times 10^{-4}$ & 144,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Mg}^c$ & Mg (HCP) & $1.5 \times 10^{-4}$ & 136,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Zn}^c$ & Zn (HCP) & $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ & 94,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Mo}^d$ & Mo (BCC) & $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ & 461,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ni}^d$ & Ni (FCC) & $1.9 \times 10^{-4}$ & 285,000 \\
\hline \multicolumn{4}{|c|}{Interdiffusion (Vacancy)} \\
\hline $\mathrm{Zn}^c$ & Cu (FCC) & $2.4 \times 10^{-5}$ & 189,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Cu}^c$ & Zn (HCP) & $2.1 \times 10^{-4}$ & 124,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Cu}^c$ & Al (FCC) & $6.5 \times 10^{-5}$ & 136,000 \\
\hline $\mathbf{M g}^{\boldsymbol{c}}$ & Al (FCC) & $1.2 \times 10^{-4}$ & 130,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Cu}^c$ & Ni (FCC) & $2.7 \times 10^{-5}$ & 256,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ni}^d{ }^d$ & Cu (FCC) & $1.9 \times 10^{-4}$ & 230,000 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}The unit of the answer is K.
response:
Using the Arrhenius equation for diffusion:

$$D = D_0 \exp\!\left(-\frac{Q_d}{RT}\right)$$

For Zn diffusing in Cu (FCC), from Table 6.2: $D_0 = 2.4\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}$, $Q_d = 189{,}000\ \mathrm{J/mol}$.

Solving for $T$:

$$T = \frac{Q_d}{R\ln(D_0/D)} = \frac{189000}{8.314\,\ln\!\left(\frac{2.4\times10^{-5}}{2.6\times10^{-16}}\right)} \approx 900\ \mathrm{K}$$

$$\boxed{900}$$
